subject: false positive on warning of specifying dsn on transformed parameters

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: false positive on warning of specifying dsn on transformed parameters
parts:
Please see the model and output from stanc below:


$ more a.stan

data {
  int J;
}
parameters {
  real y2[J, J];
}
model {
  for (j in 1:J) y2[j] ~ normal(0, 1);
}

$ stanc a.stan
Model name=a_model
Input file=a.stan
Output file=a_model.cpp
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

Warning (non-fatal):     sampling statement (~) contains a transformed parameter or local variable.
     You must increment lp__ with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
     Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
          get_base1(y2,j,"y2",1) ~ normal_log(...)


P.S. 
The warning message says left-hand-side expression, but it gives both left and right. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] false positive on warning of specifying dsn on transformed parameters
parts:
I'm glad you caught this before we had a host of
befuddled users. I just pushed a fix.

I was mistakenly checking that the index j was a
proper parameter and I should've just been checking
the expression. I was also doing the wrong thing for
binary and unary operators, so I fixed that, too.

I don't like how the indexing is printing. I should
probably have an "as written by user" expression
printer. Right now, it prints the generated C++,
which can be ugly, e.g., get_base1(y2,j,"y2",1)
instead of y2[j].

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] false positive on warning of specifying dsn on transformed parameters
parts:
On 4/28/13 3:49 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> Is it possible to avoid issuing the warning when only certain
> functions are called? E.G., right now in one of my models I get a
> bunch of warnings that look like:
>
> Warning (non-fatal): sampling statement (~) contains a transformed
> parameter or local variable.
> You must increment lp__ with the log absolute determinant of the
> Jacobian of the transform.
> Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
> col(g,gaitI) ~ normal_log(...)

We know the semantics of col() just does indexing,
so we should be able to create a symbol table of
excluded functions. But then we need to still check
inside them, because we can have usages like col(g/2, i).

For now, I think it might be better to just table this
warning message, as it's turning out to be more complicated
than I bargained for.

Program analysis is hard with a complex language!

- Bob
